dps.name: Durham Public Schools Board of Education
dps.description: Governs the public school system for Durham County, overseeing superintendent leadership, budget allocation, educational policy, and facilities.

city.name: Durham City Council
city.description: The legislative body for the City of Durham, enacting city ordinances, setting tax rates, adopting the city budget, and directing urban development and municipal services.
city.regular_schedule: 1st & 3rd Mondays at 7:00 PM (Work Sessions on Thursdays)

bocc.name: Durham Board of County Commissioners
bocc.description: The governing board of Durham County, managing county-wide services, public health, social services, property tax valuation, and local funding appropriations for DPS and Durham Tech.

members.name: Dr. Mike Lee
members.title: Chair
members.bio: Elected Chair of BOCC in December 2025. Former DPS School Board Chair. Brings deep K-12 operational expertise to county funding deliberations for schools.

members.name: Michelle Burton
members.title: Commissioner
members.bio: Former President of the Durham Association of Educators (DAE) and school librarian. Unwavering voice for public school workers and union collective bargaining.

members.name: Nida Allam
members.title: Vice Chair
members.bio: First Muslim woman elected to public office in NC. Served as BOCC Chair 2024-2025. Champions progressive labor standards, immigrant justice, and early childhood funding.

members.name: Stephen Valentine
members.title: Commissioner
members.bio: Attorney and legal educator. Focuses on criminal justice diversion, county court system modernization, veterans affairs, and transparent property appraisals.

members.name: Wendy Jacobs
members.title: Commissioner
members.bio: Longest-serving active County Commissioner (14 years). Dean of the board on climate action, farmland preservation, GoTriangle regional transit, and early childhood education.

members.name: Carl Rist
members.title: Council Member
members.bio: Longtime economic justice researcher at Prosperity Now. Focuses on living wages, municipal worker equity, wealth inequality reduction, and worker cooperatives.

members.name: Chelsea Cook
members.title: Council Member
members.bio: Legal aid attorney and tenant rights advocate. Consistently questions police technology expansions and champions tenant protections and municipal labor demands.

members.name: Javiera Caballero
members.title: Mayor Pro Tempore
members.bio: First Latina elected to Durham City Council. Mayor Pro Tem. Leading advocate for affordable housing density, immigrant inclusion, and sustainable infrastructure.

members.name: Leonardo Williams
members.title: Mayor
members.bio: Mayor of Durham, former school teacher and small business owner. Focuses on economic vibrancy, downtown revitalization, public safety partnerships, and regional transit.

members.name: Matt Kopac
members.title: Council Member
members.bio: Elected in 2025 representing Ward 1. Sustainability executive focusing on clean energy transitions, municipal carbon neutrality, and walkable urban design.

members.name: Nate Baker
members.title: Council Member
members.bio: Professional urban planner elected in 2023. Frequent dissenting voice on developer rezonings that lack binding affordability, environmental protections, and transit integration.

members.name: Shanetta Burris
members.title: Council Member
members.bio: Elected in 2025 representing Ward 2 (East Durham). Community advocate centered on neighborhood preservation, anti-displacement, and youth enrichment programs.

members.name: Bettina Umstead
members.title: Former Chair
members.bio: Served as Board Chair through the tumultuous classified salary crisis and superintendent transition. Steered board through post-pandemic recovery.

members.name: Emily Chávez
members.title: Former Board Member
members.bio: Champion of Policy 8600 (Quarterly Budget Transparency). Deeply aligned with DAE educators and Spanish-speaking immigrant communities.

members.name: Gabrielle (Gabby) Rivero
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Elected in 2026 representing District 3. Community organizer advocating for equitable school facility modernization and student mental health.

members.name: Joy Harrell-Goff
members.title: Chair
members.bio: Elected Chair of the DPS Board in July 2026. Former Vice Chair. Focuses on budget transparency, equitable school resource distribution, and classified staff compensation stability.

members.name: Millicent Rogers
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Former Durham PTA Council President and parent advocate. Prioritizes racial equity, student safety without criminalization, and transparent governance.

members.name: Nadeen Bir
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Elected in 2026 representing District 2. Longtime labor ally and public health advocate focused on worker dignity and healthcare accessibility in schools.

members.name: Natalie Bent Kitaif
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Sworn in July 2026 representing District 1. Advocate for parent engagement, multilingual family resources, and exceptional children programming.

members.name: Natalie Beyer
members.title: Former Board Member
members.bio: Served 16 years on the School Board. Consistent advocate for public school funding against state voucher expansions.

members.name: Wendell Tabb
members.title: Board Member
members.bio: Legendary Hillside High School theatre director, elected in 2024. Fierce defender of teacher retention, career and technical education, and performing arts.

members.name: Xavier Cason
members.title: Vice Chair
members.bio: Vice Chair of the School Board. Educator, arts administrator, and community organizer emphasizing fine arts in public education and restorative discipline.

meetings.title: DPS Board Regular Meeting: DAE Meet-and-Confer Resolution
meetings.executive_summary: Formal adoption of the expanded Meet-and-Confer framework with the Durham Association of Educators (DAE). Discussion of 2026-27 quarterly financial dashboard under Policy 8600.

votes.item_title: Formal Meet-and-Confer Policy Agreement with Durham Association of Educators (DAE)
votes.notes: Tabb noted support for educators but expressed concern over procedural constraints on building administrators.

disagreements.issue: Scope of Formal Meet-and-Confer Framework with DAE
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether the policy created an unmanageable grievance load for school principals or established a necessary worker voice.

arguments: Staff retention requires predictable voice in working conditions
Prevents recurring compensation miscalculations
Principals need managerial flexibility during staffing shortages

disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-1 with an annual review clause.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Meeting: Farmland Preservation & Transit Corridor Land Dedication
meetings.executive_summary: Authorization of agricultural conservation easements in northern Durham County and easement acquisitions along the NC 147 Bus Rapid Transit corridor.

votes.item_title: Northern Durham Agricultural Conservation Easements Purchase (420 Acres)
votes.notes: Preserves critical water basin watershed buffers.

meetings.title: DPS Board Annual Organizational Meeting & Officer Elections
meetings.executive_summary: Swearing in of new board members Natalie Bent Kitaif, Nadeen Bir, and Gabby Rivero. Election of Joy Harrell-Goff as Board Chair and Xavier Cason as Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Election of Board Chair: Joy Harrell-Goff
votes.notes: Unanimously elected. Joy Harrell-Goff assumes the gavel as Board Chair.

votes.item_title: Election of Vice Chair: Xavier Cason
votes.notes: Unanimous election for District 4 representative.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting: FY 2026-27 Budget & Rate Relief Fund ($682M)
meetings.executive_summary: Council approved the FY 2026-27 Municipal Budget, establishing a dedicated $4M utility rate assistance fund for low-income seniors and expanding sidewalk network paving in East Durham.

votes.item_title: Adoption of FY 2026-27 City Operating Budget ($682M)
votes.notes: Baker dissented noting unaddressed funding gaps for dedicated bike corridors.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Adoption: FY 2026-27 County Budget ($910M)
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners adopted the FY 2026-27 County Operating Budget with a 1.2-cent tax rate reduction, fully maintaining increased funding for public schools and public health nurses.

votes.item_title: Adoption of FY 2026-27 Durham County Budget ($910M) with 1.2-Cent Tax Rate Reduction
votes.notes: Unanimously enacted under Chair Dr. Mike Lee.

meetings.title: DPS Board Meeting: Rejection of School Closure Recommendations
meetings.executive_summary: Following impassioned public hearings, the Board officially rejected consultant options recommending the closure or consolidation of elementary schools for the upcoming academic year.

votes.item_title: Resolution Directing Administration to Maintain All Active Elementary Facilities for 2026-27
votes.notes: Unanimous vote protecting neighborhood elementary facilities from immediate closure.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting: Surveillance Tech & Automated License Plate Readers
meetings.executive_summary: Intense public hearing and vote on continuing contract for Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR) and acoustic gunshot detection pilot renewal.

votes.item_title: Renewal of Durham Police Dept License Plate Reader (ALPR) Inter-Agency Data Sharing
votes.notes: Sharp dissent from Cook and Baker concerning surveillance privacy, ICE data access vulnerabilities, and lack of proven crime deterrence.

disagreements.issue: Police Surveillance Technology (ALPR) vs Civil Liberties & Immigrant Protection
disagreements.summary: Debate on whether automated license plate readers assist in violent crime clearance or expose marginalized residents to unlawful surveillance.

side_a.position: Investigative Tools for Violent Crime Clearance
arguments: Police department is 20% understaffed and needs technological force multipliers
Audits showed zero unauthorized data leaks

side_b.position: Civil Liberties & Risk to Immigrant Communities
arguments: Third-party data can be subpoenaed by out-of-state anti-abortion or federal immigration agencies
Disproportionate deployment in East Durham

disagreements.resolution: Passed 4-3 with new mandatory quarterly privacy audit requirements.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Annual Reorganization & Chair Election
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners conducted their annual leadership rotation. Dr. Mike Lee was nominated and elected Chair; outgoing Chair Nida Allam was elected Vice Chair.

votes.item_title: Election of BOCC Chair: Dr. Mike Lee
votes.notes: Unanimously elected. Dr. Mike Lee assumes Chairmanship.

votes.item_title: Election of BOCC Vice Chair: Nida Allam
votes.notes: Unanimously elected.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting: Municipal Contractor Living Wage ($19.50/hr)
meetings.executive_summary: Council voted unanimously to raise the mandatory living wage threshold for all city contractors and service vendors to $19.50 per hour.

votes.item_title: City Contractor Living Wage Ordinance Indexation to $19.50/hr
votes.notes: Unanimously adopted with support from local labor coalitions.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting: FY 2025-26 Budget & HEART Expansion
meetings.executive_summary: Council adopted the $640M FY 2025-26 City Budget, funding round-the-clock 24/7 citywide expansion of the HEART non-police crisis response program, alongside step increases for AFSCME municipal workers.

votes.item_title: FY 2025-26 City Operating Budget & 24/7 HEART Program Funding ($640M)
votes.notes: Baker dissented citing an inadequate allocation for transit frequency along non-arterial bus routes.

votes.item_title: AFSCME Local 77 Municipal Worker Pay Plan & Experience Step Progression
votes.notes: Unanimously enacted after strong mobilization from sanitation and public works employees.

disagreements.issue: Transit Frequency & Sidewalk Prioritization in Capital Budget
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether capital dollars were tilted too heavily toward downtown parking deck maintenance rather than neighborhood sidewalk gaps and evening bus headways.

arguments: Downtown assets require deferred maintenance investments to support sales tax revenue
Transit-dependent residents are left waiting 45 minutes after 8 PM

disagreements.resolution: Council committed to a mid-year budget amendment for GoDurham route frequency.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Budget Adoption: DPS Supplemental Appropriation ($27M)
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners adopted the FY 2025-26 County Budget, approving a historic $27M supplemental appropriation for Durham Public Schools to guarantee living wages for classified school staff.

votes.item_title: FY 2025-26 County Budget Adoption & $27M DPS Local Supplemental Appropriation
votes.notes: Unanimous vote demonstrating county solidarity with school workers following the compensation crisis.

votes.item_title: Property Tax Rate Setting: 2.25-Cent Rate Adjustment to Support School Bond Debt
votes.notes: Valentine dissented on grounds of cumulative property tax burden on fixed-income elderly homeowners in suburban tracts.

disagreements.issue: Property Tax Rate Adjustment vs Homeowner Burden Post-Revaluation
disagreements.summary: Debate regarding the size of the ad valorem tax rate adjustment needed to service voter-approved 2022 school bonds.

arguments: Voters overwhelmingly approved bonds for Northern High and DSA
County credit rating depends on structured debt reserves

side_b.position: Tax Relief for Seniors on Fixed Incomes
arguments: Low-income seniors are being taxed out of long-held family homes

disagreements.resolution: Adopted 4-1 with an expansion of the county property tax relief circuit breaker grant.

meetings.title: DPS Board Meeting: Student Code of Conduct & Restorative Justice
meetings.executive_summary: Major policy debate on eliminating out-of-school suspensions for minor discretionary infractions and expanding campus restorative justice coordinators.

votes.item_title: Policy 4300 Revision: Elimination of Short-Term Suspensions for Discretionary Non-Violent Offenses
votes.notes: Tabb voiced caution that removing suspension tools without fully staffed restorative personnel puts too much burden on classroom teachers.

disagreements.issue: Discretionary Suspensions: Direct Class Removal vs Support Staff Readiness
disagreements.summary: Debate on whether reducing disciplinary suspensions can succeed without first funding full-time behavioral specialists in all middle schools.

arguments: Black and Brown students are suspended at 4x the rate of white peers for identical subjective infractions
Out-of-school suspension accelerates disengagement
Teachers need tools to protect classroom instructional continuity

disagreements.resolution: Approved 6-1 with phased implementation starting with K-5 schools.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Meeting: Transit Plan & Dedicated Bus Rapid Transit
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners authorized dedicated funding agreements with GoTriangle and NCDOT to advance engineering for the Durham-to-Chapel Hill bus rapid transit corridor.

votes.item_title: Durham County Half-Cent Transit Tax Allocation for BRT Engineering & Right-of-Way
votes.notes: Unanimously approved.

meetings.title: DPS Board Work Session & FY 2025-26 Budget Deliberations
meetings.executive_summary: Superintendent Dr. Anthony S. Lewis presented the preliminary operating budget request totaling $215M from county commissioners. Heated discussion on consultant contract for school consolidation study.

votes.item_title: Consultant Authorization: District-Wide Facility Utilization & Consolidation Study ($485,000)
votes.notes: Chávez and Rogers voted Nay, arguing outside consultants frequently recommend closing neighborhood schools in historically Black and Latino communities without proper community input.

disagreements.issue: School Closure/Consolidation Study: Outside Consultant Scope vs. Community Harm
disagreements.summary: Debate over hiring an outside planning consultant to identify under-enrolled facilities for consolidation.

arguments: Operating half-empty aging buildings drains instructional dollars
Independent data is necessary to withstand political scrutiny
Closures historically hollow out Black and Brown neighborhoods
The $485k should be spent directly on classroom paraprofessionals

disagreements.resolution: Motion passed 5-2 with conditions requiring public hearings in every affected high school feeder cluster.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Meeting: Downtown Transit Center RFP Award
meetings.executive_summary: Council voted to award the Downtown Transit Center mixed-use redevelopment RFP, incorporating a multistory bus depot, retail plaza, and 180 affordable housing units.

votes.item_title: Award of Downtown Durham Multi-Modal Transit Center & Mixed-Use RFP
votes.notes: Baker and Cook voted against due to private development partner having control over upper-floor market units without prevailing wage mandates.

disagreements.issue: Public Transit Land: Public-Private Partnership vs 100% Municipal Construction
disagreements.summary: Debate over whether partnering with private developers for downtown bus terminals sacrifices long-term public control.

side_a.position: Leveraging Private Capital for Modern Bus Facilities
arguments: City saves $45M in capital bond indebtedness
Provides guaranteed 180 affordable housing units steps from bus bays

side_b.position: Public Asset Ownership & Union Construction Labor
arguments: Developer retains commercial leases for 75 years
Lack of enforceable prevailing wage for construction trades

disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-2 with conditions requiring annual public progress audits.

meetings.title: Durham BOCC Regular Session: 300 E. Main St Affordable Housing
meetings.executive_summary: Commissioners approved master development agreement for 300 E. Main Street, reserving 300+ units of county-owned land strictly for households earning under 60% and 30% Area Median Income (AMI).

votes.item_title: 300 East Main Street County Land Affordable Housing Master Development Agreement
votes.notes: Unanimously passed. Hailed as a model for public land utilization for deeply affordable downtown housing.

meetings.title: DPS Board Regular Meeting: Superintendent Search Finalists
meetings.executive_summary: Board reviewed community stakeholder survey data and finalized candidate profile criteria for the permanent superintendent selection process.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Superintendent Selection Criteria & Stakeholder Matrix
votes.notes: Emphasized proven record of labor collaboration and urban district financial acumen.

meetings.title: Durham City Council Business Meeting: SCAD Text Amendments
meetings.executive_summary: Major vote on Phase 2 of the Simplified Community Assessment (SCAD) zoning amendments regarding accessory dwelling units, duplex infill, and parking minimum eliminations.

votes.item_title: SCAD Phase 2 Zoning Code Amendments: Infill Housing & Parking Minimum Reductions
votes.notes: Key ideological divide. Baker, Cook, and Burris argued the amendments enrich private developers without requiring binding 30% AMI affordability.

disagreements.issue: Market Density Infill vs Mandated Deep Affordability (SCAD)
disagreements.summary: High-stakes debate pitting supply-side urbanists who argue removing parking minimums and allowing duplexes lowers overall rent vs planning progressives who argue market-rate infill accelerates displacement in historic neighborhoods.

arguments: Restricting supply is the #1 driver of escalating housing prices in Durham
Eliminating parking mandates reduces car dependency and carbon emissions
Private capital targets vulnerable working-class neighborhoods first
Without deed-restricted 30% AMI housing, developers extract windfall profits

meetings.title: DPS Board Regular Monthly Action Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Intense deliberation regarding classified staff compensation adjustments following the comptroller audit. Board adopted interim salary supplement table and approved Policy 8600 on first reading.

votes.item_title: Policy 8600 (Quarterly Budget Transparency) — Approval on First Reading
amendments: Section 4A amended to mandate quarterly indicators publication 'within 30 days' of quarter close.
votes.notes: Unanimous approval following spirited debate regarding finance department compliance bandwidth.

votes.item_title: Classified Staff Retention Supplement Allocation ($4.2M)
votes.notes: Emergency stabilization funds for transportation and cafeteria staff.

disagreements.issue: Reporting Deadlines & Finance Staff Compliance Burden vs. Public Transparency
disagreements.summary: Deliberation over whether requiring publication strictly 'within 30 days' placed an unrealistic burden on staff during audits versus public accountability.

arguments: Staff turnover in finance makes tight 30-day deadlines risky
Could trigger default notices during end-of-year reconciliations
Community lost trust during salary crisis and requires hard deadlines
Vagueness of '30 days after' leads to endless slippage

disagreements.resolution: Amended by consensus to specify 'within 30 days' and approved unanimously on first reading.
